assessable_statement_group: Internal energy is the total kinetic energy and potential energy of the particles within a system. Kinetic energy relates to particle motion; potential energy relates to their arrangement and interactions. Temperature is related to average particle kinetic energy, not the total internal energy of a sample. A larger sample can have more internal energy at the same temperature.

assessable_statement_group: Heating increases the energy stored in a system. Within a single phase, it can raise temperature as average kinetic energy increases. During an ideal change of state, energy can instead change particle arrangements and potential energy while temperature stays constant. Follow the two worked accounts: the same input need not produce the same kind of change.
